Voat is written in a language called C#, which is a Microsoft language and requires Microsoft Windows servers (it is possible to run on Linux, but the Devs started with Windows and never sought to replace it, or didn't want to deal with the headache of getting .NET languages to run on Linux). Microsoft Windows servers are much more expensive than Linux servers due to licensing costs. Then you have bandwidth costs on top of all that, and then the monthly fees for dedicated servers. Shit ain't cheap - hell even scrimping and saving by using Linux, you'll start to lose those cost savings as your site becomes more popular, and thus has to be scaled up.

The issue is being worked on, as the platform-dependent code is being stripped out via a port to .NET Core, from which I understand makes the transition to Linux's MONO (.NET for Linux) easier.
